analysis:
The PR changes only two test files. In Qwen36ProductionCanaryTests.swift (head lines 389-391) the test event collector gains a `.toolCallDelta` case that appends `delta.completed` to toolCalls. In FlintAnswerStopTests.swift (head line 128) the test outcome recorder gains the same case. Both are exhaustive-switch updates that follow an upstream MLXLMServer enum addition. The changes touch no production code, trust boundary, key handling, attestation, authorization or encryption path, and they add no network or file I/O.

The live Qwen canary stays gated by the DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_TESTS and DARKBLOOM_LIVE_MLX_QWEN36 env vars. It disables the prefix cache (DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0) in the test bundle, so it does not exercise the T-041 SSD tier. Its hardcoded default temp paths were already present and are not part of this diff.

The test code reads only local fixtures and does not exfiltrate prompt data. I found no regression against the threat model. One unverified item remains: the production handling of the new `.toolCallDelta` event in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine lies outside this batch. If it was introduced in the same PR, its stream and tool-call paths should be reviewed separately. The delta fragments are dropped here, and only completed calls are kept. This is test-only and not a security issue.
